Subject: Draft DPA & TOMs — a couple of clarifying asks

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the initial DPA draft last week. Our legal team reviewed the TOMs exhibit and had two areas where we need clarification before we sign:

1) Key management model — we prefer a BYOK (customer-controlled key) option for EU production data. Can Redwood support a BYOK flow where Acme retains control of the master key (rotation policy to be defined)?
2) Subprocessor onboarding — can you confirm the short list of subprocessors that will have logical access to tokenized or pseudonymized data? We need a defined SLA for notification (minimum 30 days) and an opportunity to object for high-risk subprocessors.

We attached our suggested edits inline (AcmeTech_Redlines_DPA_v2.pdf). If possible, can you also confirm whether the TOMs encryption section can be expanded to specify FIPS-compliant key stores in EU regions?

Best,
Alice Moreno
Procurement Lead, AcmeTech

Subject: Re: Draft DPA & TOMs — a couple of clarifying asks

Hi Alice — thanks, appreciate the quick review and the detailed redlines. Summary answers below, full redline proposal attached.

Short answers:
- BYOK: Supported in Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) and in Dedicated for EU customers via customer-managed KMS; for Hosted we provide a "BYOK-compatible" workflow that allows key escrow with HSM integrations and role separation. We can accept the proposed rotation window but need to align on operational runbook.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a published subprocessor registry; for Acme I can list the set we expect for the first 12 months: cloud infra (eu-central-1 provider), metrics/monitoring vendor (no access to plaintext data), and a model optimization partner that only touches model weights/parameters. We commit to 30 days notice and a formal objection process in the DPA.

Actions I will take:
- Attach a revised TOMs that expands the encryption paragraph to specify FIPS-validated HSMs for EU KMS keys and a clear access control matrix for key ops (attached: Exhibit-TOMs_3.1.docx).
- Add a subprocessor notification clause matching Acme's ask and an objection workflow.
- Prepare DocuSign envelope with the final DPA and TOMs once we align.

I'll loop in Dev (sales ops) and Rishi (legal lead) to confirm commercial & KMS particulars.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft DPA & TOMs — updated redlines and objection procedure

Alice / team — attaching our updated redline and an explicit subprocessor objection procedure. Highlights:
- We added a 30-day notification + 15-day clarification period; if Acme objects, Redwood will either (a) not use that subprocessor for Acme's data, or (b) implement compensating controls agreed in writing.
- BYOK: we clarified scope — full BYOK (customer-managed key) is available for Private deployments; for Dedicated we support customer keys backed by FIPS 140-2 HSMs but require limited escrow for disaster recovery under a sealed, auditable process.
- TOMs: added explicit statements on key rotation cadence (90–180 days configurable), audit logging for key usage, and role-based access controls for key ops.

Please review the attached PDF (AcmeTech_Redlines_DPA_v2.pdf) where we track changes and include the new Exhibit-TOMs_3.1 text. If you confirm, we'll prepare DocuSign with an acceptance checkbox for the subprocessor list and an e-sign flow for the billing amendment.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Legal & Contracts, Redwood Inference
